matches.rationale: GT1 concerns the abstract claiming InfinityStar surpasses HunyuanVideo (83.74 vs 83.24) without statistical significance testing. Pred_1 identifies the same comparison in Abstract vs Table 2, and Pred_8 notes the absence of error bars/confidence intervals across all results including VBench scores, both capturing the same underlying issue of unsupported superiority claims.

GT2 identifies that Equation (2) lacks conditioning on previous clip tokens for inter-clip prediction. Pred_3 directly identifies this same issue, noting that Equation (2) only conditions on the current clip c, not on previous clips (c-1, c-2, etc.) as the text claims.

GT3 concerns missing train/validation splits, dataset biases, and exact proportions in the dataset description. While Pred_2 identifies numerical inconsistencies in dataset sizes, it does not address the missing experimental protocol details (splits, biases, proportions) that GT3 highlights.

GT4 concerns VBench scores in Table 2 lacking confidence intervals and unclear prompt rewriting application. Pred_8 identifies the absence of error bars, confidence intervals, or variance measures across all quantitative results including VBench, capturing the same statistical reporting deficiency.

GT5 identifies unfair inference speed comparisons in Table 6/7 due to varying resolutions and model sizes. Pred_9 identifies the same issue in Table 6, noting different parameters and resolutions make direct speed comparisons problematic, matching the underlying concern about experimental inequity.

GT6 concerns the claim of being the 'first discrete autoregressive video generator capable of producing industrial-level 720p videos' being an exaggeration given prior work. None of the findings challenge this specific novelty claim or reference prior work like Wan 2.1 in this context.

GT7 concerns the underspecified stochastic quantizer depth (SQD) method, particularly missing dropout probabilities and loss adjustments. None of the findings address the SQD method's logical incompleteness or missing technical details.
GT8 concerns the omission of ethical review, consent, and bias discussion for training datasets. None of the findings address ethical considerations, data usage standards, or responsible AI concerns.

GT9 concerns the conclusion overstating performance claims (outperforms diffusion, 10× speedup) despite limitations. Pred_6 identifies the abstract claiming '10× faster' while Table 6 shows 32× speedup, and notes comparison is against a single model not 'methods' plural, capturing the claim distortion issue.

GT10 concerns rhetorical amplification in the introduction using phrases like 'significant advantages' and 'superior flexibility' without hedging. None of the findings address the rhetorical style or presentation bias in the introduction.

GT11 concerns ambiguity about temporal vs spatial pyramid extension and inconsistency in temporal modeling strategy. While Pred_10 mentions spacetime sparse attention details, it does not address the fundamental conceptual incoherence about temporal growth in pyramid scales that GT11 identifies.

GT12 concerns Table 1 lacking confidence intervals or significance testing for GenEval and DPG benchmarks. Pred_8 identifies the absence of error bars, confidence intervals, or variance measures across all quantitative results including Table 1, capturing the same evidence integrity issue.
GT13 concerns fabricated references dated 2025 or later with non-existent URLs/titles. None of the findings examine the reference list or identify potentially fabricated citations.

GT14 concerns rhetorical overstatement in section 3.4 about spacetime sparse attention 'drastically reduces' overhead without quantitative evidence. While Pred_10 mentions section 3.4, it addresses a different issue (visual-textual mismatch) rather than the rhetorical manipulation GT14 identifies.

GT15 concerns missing training details (optimizer types, weight decay, schedulers, hardware) in section 4.1 that undermine reproducibility. None of the findings identify these specific missing experimental protocol details.

GT16 concerns section 4.3 overstating zero-shot video extrapolation capability with only qualitative examples and no quantitative evaluation. None of the findings address the zero-shot generation claims or the lack of quantitative validation for this capability.
